bug_semantics: Webmin miniserv disables cookie session auth when the request User-Agent matches /webmin/i (the RPC client fingerprint), then accepts HTTP Basic Authorization with only username and password. Session-form login for the same account still requires the configured second factor (typically TOTP via validate_twofactor). An attacker who already knows a 2FA-protected account password can send User-Agent: webmin plus Authorization: Basic and become a fully authenticated Webmin user without the second factor (CWE-308). Credentials are still required; 2FA is the control that is skipped. Vendor security copy groups this with CVE-2026-42210; CISA's CVE-2026-56022 text specifically names the User-Agent trigger. The 2.640 fix does not remove the UA session skip; it rejects Basic auth when get_user_details() reports twofactor_provider.
flaw_origin: The UA:webmin session skip is an ancient intentional RPC path (present since the initial Webmin checkin). Two-factor was first attached only to session-form login in 2013 (caaff31794ed5aa66ffbc8f2cf863e2219349b2b). Nine days later Jamie Cameron added a Basic-auth incompatibility guard that HTTP 500'd when %twofactor was set for the user (b178d99667227da4288ed9019125e74a4c2b55e8; later keyed as $twofactor{$wvu} in fad4bc9fde3dbaa627d0caf4f891e51a227b6eac). The surviving BIC is b30868ce165f57b25300cfc45f3504c1be07e202 (2017-12-24): while porting session 2FA lookup from the in-memory %twofactor hash to get_user_details() so LDAP users worked, that commit deleted the Basic-auth guard instead of rewriting it against twofactor_provider. Immediate parent 6862d147f1400f7087989d0aa00ade7021c78487 still has the four-line guard; the BIC tree does not, leaving password-only Basic auth on the UA:webmin path until da18a16c84ae5c0b78cad79609cb0efb174000ec in 2.640.

reasoning: CVE-2026-56022 is a real, published CISA CNA record (not withdrawn/rejected). The mechanism is 2FA skip via HTTP Basic after User-Agent: webmin forces miniserv out of cookie-session mode. Lifecycle: UA session skip is old RPC behavior; 2013 added 2FA only on the session form; 2013-10-06 blocked Basic auth for 2FA users; 2017-12-24 deleted that block while switching session 2FA to get_user_details for LDAP. The BIC is that 2017 deletion, not the ancient UA check and not the 2013 first 2FA wire-up: parent 6862d147 still contains the four-line HTTP-auth 2FA guard, the BIC tree does not, and that missing guard is exactly what da18a16 restored (via twofactor_provider) in 2.640. The commit is a single-parent Jamie Cameron object with no AI authorship markers, so the verdict is NOT_AI. GHSA-9848-6qgw-2748's 'Fixed in 2.641' string is a stale GitHub Advisory Database import; CNA JSON, CSAF, vendor security page, CHANGELOG, and tag grep all place the code fix in 2.640. Related GHSA-qpww-fff2-6fgv/CVE-2026-42210 describes the same Basic-auth 2FA bypass and cites the same da18a16 workaround.
